title: Approve an access request and provision the account in one API call
body:
## Problem
`PATCH /api/v1/admin/access-requests/{id}` with `{"status":"approved"}` only marks the request approved. It does not create a `UserAccess` profile, so the requester still has no services. The console's **Provision** action works around this by calling `PUT /api/v1/admin/users/{subject}` first and then the PATCH (`go/cmd/gateway/web/js/views/access.js`, around line 139).

This matters more now that single sign-on sign-up (`KIONGA_SIGNUP=approval`, 4b70219) files requests automatically. Verified live on 2026-10-11: approving the demo account's request through the API alone left `/api/v1/me` at `provisioned: false` and `GET /api/v1/projects` at 403. Only the extra PUT granted access.

An approved request with no profile is a state the console cannot explain. The sign-up banner falls back to "no services are assigned".

## Proposal
- Make approval atomic. `PATCH .../access-requests/{id}` with `status: approved` takes an optional grant `{role, services, project_ids, storage, compute}`. It defaults to the requested services and the sign-up resource profile, and writes the profile and the review in one transaction.
- Reject an approval that would leave no profile, or document `approved_without_profile` as an explicit state.
- The console calls the single endpoint.
- Audit one event that names both the review and the grant.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Approving through the API alone gives the requester the requested services; `/api/v1/me` reports `provisioned: true`.
- [ ] Store failure on either write leaves neither applied (both store implementations, plus a Postgres integration test).
- [ ] Console Provision uses the single call; jsdom test updated.
- [ ] Playwright: SSO sign-up, then admin approve, then the user reaches projects without signing in again.

title: End-to-end test for open sign-up mode
body:
## Problem
`KIONGA_SIGNUP=open` is covered only by Go unit tests: `TestOpenSignupProvisionsAStarterUser`, plus the domain allowlist tests in `go/internal/httpapi/signup_test.go`. No browser or live-stack test proves that a first SSO sign-in in open mode lands on a working console with the `starter` profile.

The live stack runs `approval`, and the Playwright SSO identities are fixed: GLAuth users and the Dex demo account. Once one of those identities has signed up, it never signs up again. So open mode can't be exercised by just switching the env var on the shared stack.

## Proposal
- Add an identity dedicated to the open-mode test, or a test hook that gives each run a fresh subject. For example, a GLAuth user `newcomer-<n>` from a small pool, plus an admin cleanup via `DELETE /api/v1/admin/users/{subject}` after the test.
- Run the open-mode spec against a second gateway instance (`KIONGA_SIGNUP=open`, a separate data path) in the same Compose project. Alternatively, start the gateway with an override profile in CI.
- Cover the domain allowlist end to end: an allowed verified email signs up; an outside domain gets no account and sees the "no services" banner.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A Playwright spec signs in through Dex in open mode and reaches `/api/v1/projects` with 200 on the first sign-in.
- [ ] `/api/v1/me` shows role `user`, `provisioned: true` and compute profile `starter`.
- [ ] The allowlist rejection path is covered in the browser.
- [ ] The spec is repeatable on the same stack (cleanup or fresh identity), and runs in CI with the SSO specs.
